cells.sectionSub: Transmembrane potential and thermal response computed via Schwan equation. Drag the Field Intensity slider to explore the therapeutic window.

healthy.label: Healthy Hepatocyte
healthy.description: Epithelial hepatocyte (R = 10 µm). Lower radius and thicker membrane yield higher Schwan threshold, preserved across the electroporation window targeting larger carcinoma cells.

target.label: Adenocarcinoma Cell
target.description: Carcinoma cell (R = 15 µm). Larger radius and higher membrane permittivity produce elevated transmembrane potential under identical field conditions, enabling size-selective disruption.

paramTips.radius: Cell radius R [µm] Vm scales linearly with R in the Schwan equation. Larger cells reach higher Vm under identical fields, which is the geometric basis of selective disruption.
paramTips.membraneThickness: Membrane thickness d [nm] Sets capacitance: Cm = ε_r × ε₀ / d. Thinner membranes in cancer cells raise Cm and τ, shifting the corner frequency fc downward. Typical lipid bilayer: 4–8 nm.
paramTips.dielectricConstant: Effective membrane permittivity ε_r Relative permittivity of the lipid bilayer. Determines Cm together with d. Higher values reflect altered phospholipid and cholesterol composition. Typical range: 4–10.
paramTips.conductivity: Cytoplasm conductivity σ_i [S/m] Affects the Schwan time constant τ and corner frequency fc. Higher σ_i gives shorter τ and higher fc, compressing the selective window. Typical cytoplasm: 0.3–1.0 S/m.
paramTips.thresholdVoltage: Electroporation threshold Vth [V] Transmembrane potential above which irreversible pore formation is initiated. Disruption ratio is DR = Vm / Vth. Literature range: 0.5–2.0 V.
paramTips.resonantFreqGHz: Capsid resonance frequency [GHz] Fundamental acoustic resonance of the cell wall or viral capsid, set by shell geometry and the cytoplasm speed of sound. Bacteria: 0.3–2 GHz; viruses: 5–20 GHz.
paramTips.capsidQ: Acoustic quality factor Q Sets the sharpness of the resonance peak: half-power bandwidth = f_res / Q. Bacteria: Q ≈ 3–4 (peptidoglycan viscous damping). Protein-capsid viruses: Q ≈ 25–30.

cells.paramsToggleTip: Cell Parameters Edit biophysical properties that drive the Schwan equation calculation in real time. Changes immediately update Vm, selectivity, and the frequency response chart.
cells.paramsToggleTipAcoustic: Cell Parameters Edit acoustic and structural properties that drive the capsid resonance model in real time. Changes immediately update disruption ratio and the frequency response chart.
cells.derivedTip: Derived biophysical parameters Computed in real time from the editable values above. Cm = ε_r × ε₀ / d Membrane specific capacitance [mF/m²] τ = R·Cm·(2σ_e+σ_i) / (2σ_e·σ_i) Schwan time constant (Kotnik & Miklavcic 2000) Sets the frequency roll-off fc = 1/(2πτ) Characteristic frequency, Vm drops −3 dB here Below fc: quasi-DC regime, Vm at maximum
cells.derivedTipAcoustic: Acoustic resonance constants Computed from the capsid model parameters. τ = R·Cm·(2σ_e+σ_i) / (2σ_e·σ_i) Schwan time constant (electrical coupling) fc = 1/(2πτ) Schwan corner frequency (electrical roll-off) BW = f_res / Q Half-power bandwidth of the acoustic resonance peak Narrower BW: higher frequency selectivity
cells.resetBtnTip: Reset to Preset Defaults Restores all parameters to the original values for this preset. Useful after editing to explore changes.

slider.title: Field Control
slider.tipSnapFcH:
Snap frequency to healthy cell corner frequency fc(H) = {fc}
At fc: Vm drops to 1/√2 of quasi-DC peak. Useful for selective τ measurement.
slider.tipSnapFcT:
Snap frequency to target cell corner frequency fc(T) = {fc}
At fc: Vm drops to 1/√2 of quasi-DC peak. Useful for selective target disruption studies.
slider.orientationSub: θ = 0° (field-aligned) maximises Vm · cos(θ) cancels in selectivity ratio
slider.lysisNSub: N × (t_p / dc) = total protocol time above threshold
slider.doubleShellSub: Kotnik & Miklavcic (2006) · bandpass nuclear Vm · f_peak ≈ 0.7-2 MHz
slider.tipMinPulse: Minimum pulse width, 3τ rule Full membrane charging requires t_p ≥ 3τ (≥95% plateau). Green: full charging · Amber: partial (τ - 3τ) · Red: sub-threshold (<τ) τ = R·Cm·(2σ_e+σ_i)/(2σ_e·σ_i) [Kotnik & Miklavcic 2000]

regime.tipElectrolytic: Electrolytic Regime (<300 MHz) Below the dielectric relaxation frequency of saline (~338 MHz), the medium behaves as a conductor and direct-contact electrodes work well. Hardware: electroporation cuvette · pulse generator · direct wire connection DC impedance model (Z = d/σA) is valid in this regime. Ref: Foster & Schwan (1989) CRC Crit. Rev. Biomed. Eng.
regime.tipNearfieldRf: Near-field RF Regime (300 MHz-1 GHz) Above ~338 MHz the medium transitions from conductor to lossy dielectric. Direct electrodes still work for short path lengths, but skin depth (~13-41 mm) starts to limit penetration. Hardware: coaxial RF probe · impedance-matched coaxial cable · 50 Ω system DC impedance model is approximate, use transmission-line or FEM for accuracy. Ref: Gabriel et al. (1996) Phys. Med. Biol. 41:2271
regime.tipMicrowave: Microwave Regime (>1 GHz) Skin depth falls below 13 mm. DC electrode coupling is ineffective , only the surface of the sample is accessible. Hardware: rectangular waveguide · resonant cavity · horn antenna Field uniformity is a major challenge. Cuvette geometry sets up standing waves. GHz frequencies are required for acoustic capsid resonance (bacteria/virus). Ref: Gabriel et al. (1996); Tsen et al. (2007) J. Biol. Phys.

exp.tipThDepH: H Re[K], Healthy DEP Clausius-Mossotti factor Re[K(f)] for the healthy cell at log-time frequency. Re[K] > 0 → pDEP (attracted to field maxima) Re[K] < 0 → nDEP (repelled from field maxima) Hidden in resonance mode (model invalid at GHz).

exp.zDriftTip: ⚗ Impedance Drift Detected Medium conductivity has shifted from baseline by more than 5%. This typically indicates ion release from lysing target cells. Click to open the Instrument Panel for real-time impedance tracking and corrected field voltage.

resonance.chartNote: Disruption ratio = (E / E_thr) × L(f, f_res, Q)
resonance.noteBody: Acoustic/mechanical capsid & cell-wall disruption. f_res ≈ v_protein/(2R): viral capsids ~10-12 GHz, bacterial walls ~0.5-1.5 GHz. Mammalian cells (R ≈ 10 µm) have no GHz resonance, frequency-selective disruption. Ref: Tsen et al. (2007); Dykeman & Sankey (2008)
resonance.noResonance: No resonance parameters for this cell
resonance.tipFieldFormula: Disruption ratio = (E / E_threshold) × L(f, f_res, Q)
resonance.tipTargetBadgeNote: ≥100% at resonance → capsid/cell-wall disruption threshold exceeded
resonance.tipHealthyBadgeBody:
Mammalian cells lack rigid-shell resonance, Schwan Vm → 0 at GHz (ωτ ≫ 1).
At f_res(target) in GHz, healthy cell disruption ≈ 0.

log.tipLogReading: Log Reading Capture a snapshot of the current field parameters, cell Vm values, disruption ratios, and temperatures. Appended to the session table and exportable as CSV.
log.tipExportCsv: Export CSV Download all logged readings as a comma-separated spreadsheet. Each row contains frequency, field, Vm, disruption ratios, temperatures, and event type.
log.tipClearLog: Clear Log Remove all entries from the current session. This cannot be undone.
log.tipThNumber: Reading # Sequential index within the current session. Resets to 1 when the log is cleared.
log.tipThTime: Timestamp Local time (HH:mm:ss) when the reading was logged.
log.tipThFreq: RF Frequency (kHz) Carrier frequency applied at the time of this reading.
log.tipThField: Field Intensity (V/cm) Applied electric field at the time of this reading.
log.tipThTargetVm: Target Vm (mV) Transmembrane potential of the target cell computed via the Schwan equation.
log.tipThHealthyVm: Healthy Vm (mV) Transmembrane potential of the healthy reference cell.
log.tipThSel: Selectivity (×) Target-Vm / Healthy-Vm ratio at the time of logging. ≥{strong}×, strong window · ≥{marginal}×, marginal
log.tipThEvent: Event Type 'manual', user-triggered reading 'lysis', triggered automatically at lysis threshold
log.tipCellFreq: Frequency: {freq} kHz Carrier frequency at the time of this reading.
log.tipCellField: Field Intensity: {field} V/cm Applied electric field at the time of this reading.
log.tipCellTargetVm: Target Vm: {vm} mV Cell: {preset} Disruption ratio: {ratio}% of lysis threshold
log.tipCellHealthyVm: Healthy Vm: {vm} mV Disruption ratio: {ratio}% of lysis threshold
log.tipCellSel: Selectivity: ×{sel} Target-Vm / Healthy-Vm ratio at this reading. Target temp: {targetTemp} °C · Healthy temp: {healthyTemp} °C
log.tipCellLysis: Lysis Event Cell membrane disruption threshold was exceeded. This reading was auto-logged at the lysis trigger.
log.tipCellManual: Manual Reading User-triggered snapshot of the current field state.
log.tipDose: Cumulative Dose Specific energy absorbed (J/kg) estimated from SAR and pulse duty cycle across all logged readings. Approximation only, ignores blood perfusion and heat loss.

drChart.title: Disruption Ratio: f-Domain
drChart.tipTitle: Disruption Ratio vs Frequency Shows DR(f) = Vm(f) / Vthreshold × PEF for both cells. Green region: therapeutic window, target DR ≥ 85% while healthy DR < 50%. Dashed amber line = reversible EP boundary (50%). Dashed red line = lysis threshold (85%).
drChart.sectionTip: DR(f) = Vm·PEF / Vm_thr, Amber dashed = Rev-EP 50% · Red dashed = Lysis 85% · Green fill = therapeutic window (target ≥ 85%, healthy < 50%)
